examples.en: During the day, a babysitter looks after the child.
I had to go out in the evening, so I found a babysitter.

examples.ko: 베이비시터 구하는 앱을 써 본 적 있어요?
examples.en: Have you ever used an app for finding a babysitter?

examples.ko: 우리 아이는 베이비시터 이모를 잘 따라요.
examples.en: My child follows the babysitter auntie well.
I left my contact information with the babysitter.
When I was a college student, I worked as a babysitter every vacation.

explain: 집에서 아이를 돌봐 주는 사람을 말하는 외래어예요. 같은 일을 하는 사람을 '아이 돌보미'나 '보모'라고도 해요. 아이를 맡기는 일 자체는 '아이를 맡기다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The child caregiver comes in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '베이비시터'와 같은 일을 하는 사람을 한국어로 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A Korean-word way to refer to the same job as a babysitter.

phrases.en: I leave my child with the babysitter in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아이를 맡기는 상황에서 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for leaving a child in someone's care.
phrases.en_equiv: to leave the child with a babysitter

phrases.en: The babysitter is coming tomorrow morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 집으로 돌봐 주러 오는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the person who comes to your home to look after the child.

explain_en: This loanword refers to a person who looks after children at home. People doing the same job are also called '아이 돌보미' or '보모'. Leaving a child in someone's care is '아이를 맡기다'.

examples.en: This book is for children, so the print is big.

examples.ko: 아동용 의자를 식당에서 빌릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can borrow a children's chair at the restaurant.

examples.ko: 이 약은 아동용과 어른용이 따로 있어요.
examples.en: This medicine comes in separate versions for children and adults.
Children's toothbrushes have soft bristles.
I went to the store to buy a children's bike.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 아동용이 아니라서 아이와 보기 어려워요.
examples.en: This movie isn't for children, so it is hard to watch with a kid.

explain: '어린이용'과 같은 뜻인데, 상품 표시나 설명에서는 '아동용'이 더 자주 보여요. 짝이 되는 말은 '어른용'이에요.

phrases.en: This toothbrush is for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아동용'과 같은 뜻이고, 말할 때 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 아동용, and more common in speech.

phrases.en: Children's toothbrushes are small.
phrases.nuance_ko: '아동용' 뒤에 물건 이름을 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put an item name after 아동용.

phrases.en: This movie is not for children.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어린이에게 맞지 않는다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say something is not suitable for kids.

explain_en: It means the same as '어린이용', but '아동용' is seen more on product labels and descriptions. The opposite is '어른용' (for adults).

examples.en: I'm still an amateur, but I practice hard.
That photographer is an amateur, but her skill is outstanding.
I won a prize for the first time at an amateur competition.
I was embarrassed to make such an amateur mistake.
Every weekend I play on an amateur soccer team.
Amateurs and pros differ starting from the amount of practice.

explain: 반대말은 '프로'예요. 취미로 하는 사람을 말할 때는 중립적이지만 '아마추어 같다'고 하면 서툴다고 깎아내리는 말이 돼요. 그래서 일터에서 사람에게 '아마추어 같아요'라고 하면 실례예요.

phrases.en: I entered the competition as an amateur player.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 받고 하지 않는 선수를 중립적으로 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A neutral term for a player who doesn't compete professionally.

phrases.example: 우리 동네 아마추어 팀과 경기를 했어요.
phrases.en: We played a game against our neighborhood amateur team.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취미로 모여 운동하는 팀을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A team that plays as a hobby.

phrases.en: If you say it like that, it sounds amateurish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서툴다고 깎아내리는 말이 되니 사람에게는 조심해서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This puts someone down as clumsy, so be careful using it about people.

explain_en: Its opposite is '프로'. For someone who does something as a hobby it is neutral, but saying someone is 'like an amateur' puts down their clumsiness. So calling a coworker '아마추어 같아요' is rude.

en: to be emotionally moved; to be touched

examples.en: I was really moved after watching the movie.

examples.ko: 친구가 쓴 편지를 읽고 감동한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I was once touched after reading a letter my friend wrote.
I was moved by the song and cried.
I'm easily moved even by small kindnesses.

examples.ko: 그 이야기를 읽으면 누구나 감동할 거예요.
examples.en: Anyone who reads that story will be moved.

examples.ko: 이런 선물에도 감동하지 않는 사람이 있어요?
examples.en: Is there anyone who isn't touched by a gift like this?

explain: 사람이 주어이면 '감동하다'나 '감동받다'를 쓰고, 영화나 이야기가 주어이면 '감동적이다'를 써요. '영화가 감동적이에요', '저는 감동했어요'처럼 짝을 맞춰 보세요. '감동을 받았어요'도 아주 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 저는 그 노래를 듣고 감동을 받았어요.
phrases.en: I was moved when I heard that song.
phrases.nuance_ko: '감동하다'와 뜻이 같고, 말할 때 아주 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 감동하다 and very common in speech.

phrases.en: I was really touched by my friend's gift.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거형으로, 마음이 움직인 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The past form, used for being emotionally moved.

phrases.en: This movie is really moving.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 이야기가 주어일 때 쓰는 형용사 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An adjective form used when a movie or story is the subject.

explain_en: When a person is the subject, use '감동하다' or '감동받다'; when a movie or story is the subject, use '감동적이다'. Compare '영화가 감동적이에요' and '저는 감동했어요'. '감동을 받았어요' is also very common.

examples.en: In summer, cold soup brings back your appetite.
I floated ice in the cold soup and ate it.
I put julienned cucumber into the cold soup.
The cold soup was so refreshing that I finished my rice quickly.
Please give me one more bowl of cold soup.
My mother made me cold soup.

explain: 차갑게 먹는 국이라서 따뜻한 국과 달라요. 오이냉국, 미역냉국처럼 앞에 재료 이름을 붙여서 많이 말해요. 여름 식탁에서 자주 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: On hot days, I want to eat cold cucumber soup.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오이로 만든 대표적인 여름 냉국이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical summer cold soup made with cucumber.

phrases.en: I made cold seaweed soup for lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 미역으로 만든 냉국이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cold soup made with seaweed.

phrases.en: In summer, I eat cold soup with rice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 국을 먹는다고 할 때 '먹다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 먹다 for eating soup.

explain_en: It is a soup eaten cold, unlike a hot soup. People often put the main ingredient before it, as in 오이냉국 (cucumber) and 미역냉국 (seaweed). You see it often on summer tables.

en: to be rather embarrassed; to be rather bewildered; to be rather disconcerted

examples.en: My name was suddenly called, and I was flustered.

examples.ko: 모르는 사람이 말을 걸어서 좀 당황스러워요.
examples.en: A stranger talked to me, and I'm a bit flustered.

examples.ko: 약속 장소를 잘못 알았다니 당황스러운 일이에요.
examples.en: It's a bewildering thing to have the wrong meeting place.
Much to my dismay, I left my wallet at home.

examples.ko: 면접에서 예상 못 한 질문을 받으면 당황스럽지요.
examples.en: It's disconcerting to get a question you didn't expect in an interview.

examples.ko: 친구가 갑자기 화를 내서 당황스럽다고 느꼈어요.
examples.en: My friend suddenly got angry and I felt thrown off.

explain: '당황하다'는 놀라서 어쩔 줄 모르는 사람의 모습이고, '당황스럽다'는 상황이 그런 마음이 들게 한다는 느낌이에요. '황당하다'는 어이가 없을 때, '당황스럽다'는 어떻게 해야 할지 모를 때 써요.

phrases.example: 비행기를 놓친 건 정말 당황스러운 상황이었어요.
phrases.en: Missing the plane was a really bewildering situation.
phrases.nuance_ko: '당황스럽다'를 '-ㄴ' 꼴로 바꿔 '상황', '일'을 꾸며 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective changes to its -ㄴ form to describe 상황 or 일.

phrases.en: My friend who was asked the question looked flustered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 그렇게 보인다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say someone looks that way from the outside.

phrases.en: The lights suddenly went out and everyone was flustered.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 놀라서 어쩔 줄 모르는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person who is so startled they do not know what to do.

explain_en: '당황하다' describes a person who is startled and at a loss, while '당황스럽다' says the situation makes you feel that way. '황당하다' is for absurd things that leave you speechless; '당황스럽다' is for not knowing what to do.

examples.en: My father works as a professor at a university in the provinces.
To become a university professor, you need a doctorate.
When I was young, I dreamed of becoming a professor.
He is a famous professor, so he gives many lectures.
I sent my question to the professor by email.
The professor's office is on the fourth floor.

explain: 직업을 말할 때는 '대학교수'를 쓰고, 직접 부를 때는 '교수님'이라고 해요. 이름 뒤에도 '김 교수님'처럼 '교수님'을 붙여요. '선생님'보다 '교수님'이 대학에서는 더 정확한 호칭이에요.

phrases.en: Professor, I have a question.
phrases.nuance_ko: 대학교수를 직접 부를 때는 '교수님'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used when addressing a university professor directly.

phrases.en: Professor Kim's class is interesting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성 뒤에 '교수님'을 붙여 존경을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 교수님 after the surname shows respect.

phrases.en: I want to become a university professor someday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 직업을 목표로 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase for talking about a career goal.

explain_en: Use '대학교수' to name the job, but when addressing the person, say '교수님'. After a surname you attach '교수님' too, as in '김 교수님'. At a university, '교수님' is the more accurate title than '선생님'.

examples.ko: 비가 그친 뒤 길에 물웅덩이가 많이 생겼어요.
examples.en: After the rain stopped, many puddles formed on the road.
The child jumped over a small puddle.

examples.ko: 운전할 때 물웅덩이 옆을 지나면 물이 튀어요.
examples.en: When driving, water splashes if you pass next to a puddle.
The kids splashed around in the puddle.
The sky was reflected in the puddle, and it looked pretty.
Please be careful and go around the puddles.

explain: 그냥 '웅덩이'라고 해도 되지만, 비 온 뒤 고인 물을 분명히 말할 때 '물웅덩이'를 써요. '밟다, 튀다, 피하다, 뛰어넘다'와 자주 같이 나와요.

phrases.en: I stepped in a puddle by mistake and my socks got wet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웅덩이에 발을 넣게 되었을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when your foot lands in a puddle.

phrases.example: 신발이 젖을까 봐 물웅덩이를 피해서 걸었어요.
phrases.en: I walked around the puddles so my shoes wouldn't get wet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비 온 뒤 길을 걸을 때 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when walking after rain.

phrases.example: 비가 오면 이 길에는 물웅덩이가 생겨요.
phrases.en: When it rains, puddles form on this road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비가 와서 물이 고였다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to say water collected after rain.

explain_en: You can just say '웅덩이', but '물웅덩이' makes clear it is standing water, like after rain. It often appears with verbs like 밟다, 튀다, 피하다 and 뛰어넘다.

examples.ko: 옥상에 있는 물탱크를 이번 주에 청소해요.
examples.en: They are cleaning the water tank on the roof this week.

examples.ko: 물탱크에 물이 얼마나 남았는지 확인해 보세요.
examples.en: Please check how much water is left in the tank.

examples.ko: 캠핑카 뒤쪽에 작은 물탱크가 달려 있어요.
examples.en: A small water tank is attached at the back of the camper.

examples.ko: 이 물탱크는 오래돼서 곧 바꿔야 해요.
examples.en: This water tank is old, so we need to replace it soon.

examples.ko: 비가 안 와서 물탱크의 물이 거의 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: It hasn't rained, so the tank is almost out of water.

examples.ko: 물탱크 청소하는 날에는 물이 잠깐 끊겨요.
examples.en: On the day the tank is cleaned, the water is cut off for a while.

explain: 건물 옥상이나 지하, 캠핑카 등에 물을 모아 두는 통을 말해요. 건물 설비로는 '저수조'라는 말도 쓰지만, 일상 대화에서는 '물탱크'가 편하게 들려요.

phrases.en: We clean the water tank next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 건물에서 정기적으로 하는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for regular maintenance in a building.

phrases.en: It rained, so the water tank is full.
phrases.nuance_ko: 탱크에 물이 넘칠 만큼 있다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means the tank holds as much water as it can.

phrases.en: I filled the camper's water tank with water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물을 넣어서 채우는 동작을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the action of filling it with water.

explain_en: It is a container that stores water on a building's roof or basement, or in a camper. Buildings also use the term '저수조', but '물탱크' sounds more natural in everyday talk.

examples.en: There are many strange fish in the deep sea.
I learned to dive to see under the sea in person.

examples.ko: 바닷속은 소리가 거의 안 들려서 아주 조용해요.
examples.en: There is almost no sound under the sea, so it is very quiet.

examples.ko: 친구가 찍어 준 바닷속 사진이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The underwater photos my friend took are really pretty.
I saw a huge turtle under the sea off Jeju Island.
The deeper you go, the darker it gets under the sea.

explain: '바다 속'처럼 띄지 않고 '바닷속'으로 붙여 써요. 비슷한 '물속'은 수영장이나 강에도 쓰지만 바닷속은 바다에만 써요. '땅속', '산속'도 같은 방식으로 만든 말이에요.

phrases.en: The deep sea is very dark and quiet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 형용사 '깊은'과 함께 써서 바다 아래 깊은 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Paired with the adjective 깊은 to mean the deep part under the sea.

phrases.en: I met a big turtle under the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: '에서'를 붙여 바다 아래에서 일어나는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에서 to talk about things that happen under the sea.

phrases.en: The world under the sea is really amazing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닷속 풍경이나 생물 이야기를 할 때 '바닷속 + 명사'로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use 바닷속 + noun when talking about scenery or life under the sea.

explain_en: It is written as one word, '바닷속', not '바다 속'. The similar '물속' (in the water) also works for pools and rivers, but 바닷속 is only for the sea. '땅속' (underground) and '산속' (deep in the mountains) are made the same way.

examples.en: Lights came on one by one on the night street outside the window.
Unlike in the daytime, the night streets are quiet and lonely.
I walked the night streets with a friend and we talked.
This neighborhood's streets are well lit at night, so it's safe.

examples.ko: 비 오는 밤거리 풍경이 영화 같았어요.
examples.en: The scene of the street at night in the rain was like a movie.
Shall we head out to the night streets after dinner?

explain: '야경'은 밤에 보이는 경치 전체이고, '밤거리'는 거리 자체를 가리켜요. '밤거리를 걷다', '밤거리를 헤매다'처럼 걷거나 돌아다니는 동작과 잘 어울려요.

phrases.en: After dinner, I walked along the night streets.
phrases.nuance_ko: 천천히 거리를 걷는 모습에 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits a slow walk down the street.

phrases.en: I wandered around the night streets during my trip.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목적 없이 여기저기 다닌다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Suggests roaming around without a set goal.

phrases.en: Only footsteps could be heard on the quiet night street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 적은 밤의 거리를 그릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe a night street with few people.

explain_en: '야경' is the whole night view, while '밤거리' points to the street itself. It pairs well with walking or wandering verbs, as in '밤거리를 걷다' and '밤거리를 헤매다'.
